relevance_note: The letter describes identifiable individuals with a germline TNFAIP3 variant: "Here, we report a Japanese family containing two cases of autoinflammatory disease which exhibit an identical novel TNFAIP3 mutation."
method_note: No script was used; every row and span was hand-copied from the Markdown. IMPORTANT: this paper's Markdown contains U+2009 THIN SPACE between a number and its unit (e.g. '11 years', '14 years', '2 years prior', 'prior 3 years', 'c597-598 T deletion', 'TNF-α-stimulation (24 h)'); those spans are written in this JSON with the escape \u2009 so that the decoded string matches the paper character for character. Other spaces (e.g. '0.55 mg/dL (<0.30)') are ordinary spaces. This is a single-family case report (letter). In scope: the proband ('the patient'), his mother (deceased, symptomatic), his younger sister (same variant), his father (tested, no TNFAIP3 variant) and his younger brothers (sequence analysis not possible). The paper says 'younger brothers' in the plural without a number, so one row 'younger brother of the patient' stands for them; no count was invented. Labels: the paper's only labels are the role words 'the proband'/'the patient', so the single unnamed patient of a case report is labelled 'patient' and relatives '<relation as written> of the patient'. Contradictions found in the paper: (1) the variant is printed 'C596_598 del A' in the text but 'c597-598 T deletion' in the Fig. 1 legend; (2) the Discussion calls it 'a novel heterozygous missense mutation' although the text and legend describe a frameshift with a premature stop, so variant_type_as_stated is recorded as 'frameshift' (stated twice); (3) the proband is 'a 17-year-old Japanese boy' at referral with a 3-year history yet is admitted 'Three years later', so no age at last evaluation is recorded (age_at_onset comes from 'the disease onset (at 14 years old)'). Inheritance was left 'not reported': the paper only reports the father's negative test, 'suggesting that these mutations were maternally derived'; the mother was not tested and no parent is stated to carry the variant. pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors is 'novel' because the authors use no formal class (pathogenic/VUS). The variant cDNA-like string is printed without a 'c.' prefix, so cdna_hgvs_as_stated is null and the string is kept in variant_original_string. No stacked (' / ') cells occur in this paper. Additional file 1 Table S1 gives the proband's laboratory values, but its converted cells contain long irregular runs of spaces, so only main-text quotes were used and no supplement-derived row was created. Two judgement calls to flag: (a) the proband's row 'no abnormalities' records the paper's whole-investigation statement ('There were no abnormalities except elevated levels of CRP') exactly as printed, because it names no single abnormality and so excludes nothing more specific; (b) the sister's only feature is 'similar symptoms', which the paper does not itemise, so it is kept in phenotypic_features as stated but mapped to no checklist item (all her checklist rows are 'not reported'). The father ('unaffected'/'healthy') and the brothers ('without symptoms') have no individual features: no phenotypic_features rows, all checklist items 'not reported'. No prior report of these patients is stated, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false with no span.
